question.problem:
Suppose $a=[1,\,2]^{T}$ and $b=[-1,\,-1]^{T}.$ Find the Manhattan distance between $a$ and $b.$

${d}_{1}(a,b)=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Manhattan distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{1}(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{1}
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{1}={\sum }_{i=1}^{N}|{v}_{i}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{1}(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{1} \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]‖}_{1} \\  & =|1-(-1)|+|2-(-1)| \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
